title: US PCE nowcast – Slow progress in easing inflation in July
gist: Oxford Economics nowcasts July headline PCE inflation easing only slightly to 3.6% with core steady at 3.3%, and expects September methodological revisions to push core down to 3%, but sticky shelter and portfolio-management-fee costs keep the Fed on hold until inflation nears 2% in late 2027.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics nowcasts July headline PCE inflation decreasing only marginally to 3.6%, while core PCE inflation holds steady at 3.3%.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Only marginal disinflation in the Fed's preferred gauge argues against near-term rate cuts and supports a higher-for-longer rates stance.
insights.quote: Headline PCE inflation is expected to decrease marginally to 3.6%, while core PCE inflation holds steady at 3.3%.
insights.locator: Inflation remains a pressing concern, with the PCE index showing only slight progress in July.

insights.claim: Lower energy prices are exerting downward pressure on inflation, but their effect on the PCE index is limited compared to their effect on CPI.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Investors should expect PCE to understate energy-driven disinflation relative to CPI, meaning CPI prints may look better than the Fed's actual policy gauge.
insights.quote: Lower energy prices have exerted downward pressure, but their impact on the PCE index is limited compared to the CPI.
insights.locator: Lower energy prices have exerted downward pressure

insights.claim: Methodological changes due in September are expected to reveal a more favourable inflation picture, potentially revising July core PCE inflation down to 3%.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Watch for a data-driven, non-organic step-down in core PCE in September that could shift market rate-cut expectations even without real disinflation progress.
insights.quote: Methodological changes in September are anticipated to reveal a more favourable inflation outlook, potentially revising core inflation down to 3% for July.
insights.locator: Methodological changes in September are anticipated

insights.claim: Persistent inflationary pressures from shelter costs and portfolio management fees will keep the Federal Reserve cautious despite the anticipated methodological improvement in the inflation reading.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Sticky shelter and services (portfolio fee) components are the key sub-indices to track for the Fed's reaction function, more so than headline energy-driven moves.
insights.quote: persistent inflationary pressures—particularly from shelter costs and portfolio management fees—will keep the Federal Reserve cautious
insights.locator: Despite these adjustments, persistent inflationary pressures

insights.claim: With the labour market stable, Oxford Economics expects significant Fed rate hikes are unlikely until late 2027, when inflation may approach the Fed's 2% target.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Positions investors for an extended higher-for-longer rate regime lasting into late 2027 rather than near-term policy shifts.
insights.quote: The labour market remains stable, suggesting that significant rate hikes are unlikely until late 2027, when inflation may approach the Fed’s 2% target.
